questions.question: Why do people work?
options: To earn money for everyday life and fulfill their responsibilities
questions.explanation: People work to earn money for everyday life - food, housing, clothes and other needs.

questions.question: Chrumko notices that mom is getting ready for work in the morning. Why does she work even when it's raining?
options: To earn money from her work, which allows the family to pay for rent, food and school supplies
questions.explanation: Mom must go to work because she earns money, which allows the family to pay for everything they need.

questions.question: What role do people's jobs have in society?
options: They help others - teach, heal, repair, manufacture, provide services
questions.explanation: Many people help others through their work. Every job has value because it contributes to society's functioning.

questions.question: Work helps provide many things that families use every day and consider normal.
questions.explanation: Work is the source of financial resources needed for daily life.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Work has value based on its type for society.
Work is pointless and nobody spends time on it.
questions.explanation: Work is not pointless - it's essential for society's functioning and individual survival.

questions.question: Match the type of work with its contribution to society.
questions.explanation: Each job has a specific role in society.

questions.question: Sort different aspects of work into correct groups.
questions.explanation: Work has multiple aspects - both financial and social.

questions.question: Put in order what Chrumko gradually realizes about work.
orderItems: Mom prepares for work in the morning
Chrumko notices that mom works even in bad weather
Chrumko understands that work is why the family has a home and food
Chrumko realizes that work is important for the whole family
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the relationship between work and daily life.

questions.question: Do all adults do the same work?
options: Yes, everyone does the same thing
No, people do different jobs based on experience and skills
questions.explanation: People do different jobs based on what they know, what they enjoy, and what society needs.

questions.question: Chrumko goes to school in the morning. How many different jobs does he see?
options: Bus driver, teacher, road workers and others in the shop and post office
questions.explanation: Chrumko sees how many different people work - driver, teacher, workers, shop assistant, postman and others.

questions.question: There are occupations where people make things, repair them, teach, or heal.
questions.explanation: Jobs can be divided by type of activity - manufacturing, repairs, education, healthcare, etc.

questions.question: Match the job with the type of activity.
questions.explanation: Different occupations deal with different types of activities.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: People do different jobs based on experience.
All adults do exactly the same thing.
Differences in occupations reflect people's talents and interests.
questions.explanation: Not everyone does the same - there's great diversity in jobs.

questions.question: Sort occupations by type.
questions.explanation: Occupations can be categorized by their focus.

questions.question: Why is it important to have different occupations?
options: They complement each other and together help the world function
questions.explanation: Each occupation has its purpose. All different jobs complement each other and together help the world function.

questions.question: Does everyone earn the same money for their work?
options: No, salary depends on the type of work, experience and responsibility
questions.explanation: Salary depends on the type of work, experience, responsibility and time spent on the job.

questions.question: Everyone receives salary regularly, usually once a month into their bank account.
questions.explanation: Workers receive salary in regular intervals, most commonly monthly.

questions.question: Chrumko talks with his father about salaries. What does father say?
options: He receives salary once a month and from it the family pays for everything needed
questions.explanation: Father explains that he receives salary once a month and from this money the family pays for everything during the whole month.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Salary amount depends on the type of work and experience.
Everyone receives the same salary regardless of occupation.
Salary is paid regularly, usually monthly.
questions.explanation: Salaries differ - not everyone earns the same amount.

questions.question: Match the factor with its influence on salary.
matchRight: Higher position usually means higher salary
People with more years in job earn more
Longer work hours can mean higher income
questions.explanation: Multiple factors influence the level of salary.

questions.question: Sort factors by whether they increase salary or have no effect.
questions.explanation: Professional development increases a worker's value and salary.

questions.question: Why is it important to spend salary wisely?
options: Because salary must cover all necessities for the entire month
Because everything can be bought immediately
questions.explanation: Money from work must be divided wisely to last a longer time.

questions.question: Why is time important in work?
options: A person earns money based on the time they spend working
questions.explanation: In many jobs, a person earns money based on time worked - the more hours, the bigger the reward.

questions.question: Chrumko sees his older brother working for neighbors. What does he do?
options: Helps all morning - gathering leaves, raking grass, carrying branches
questions.explanation: Brother works over the weekend all morning. They work together and invest time and effort.

questions.question: Reward for work is directly related to time and effort a person puts in.
questions.explanation: The more time and effort, the bigger the reward.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Time affects the amount of reward for work.
Number of hours worked has no effect on pay.
questions.explanation: Number of hours has a huge effect on pay - it's a basic principle of wages.

questions.question: Match hours with type of work arrangement.
questions.explanation: Different amounts of time are paid according to different criteria.

questions.question: Sort activities by time they take.
questions.explanation: Different activities take different amounts of time.

questions.question: Put in order what Chrumko realizes about time and money.
orderItems: Chrumko sees that his older brother works for several hours
Brother receives a reward after finishing work
Chrumko understands that more hours mean more money
Chrumko realizes that time is valuable in work
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the value of time in work.

questions.question: What is productivity?
options: How much work a person can accomplish in a certain time
questions.explanation: Productivity means how much work a person can accomplish in a certain time. If they work concentrated, they do more in less time.

questions.question: Chrumko is doing homework. First day he keeps looking at his phone. What happens?
options: Homework takes him a short time
Homework takes him a very long time because he gets distracted
questions.explanation: Homework takes very long because he's constantly distracted and interrupts work.

questions.question: Concentration and working without interruptions increases productivity.
questions.explanation: Concentrated work without interruptions is always more efficient.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Distractions improve the quality of work.
questions.explanation: Distractions never increase productivity - they do the opposite.

questions.question: Match activity with its effect on productivity.
questions.explanation: Different factors affect productivity differently.

questions.question: Sort factors by their effect on productivity.
questions.explanation: Environment has a big effect on the ability to work efficiently.

questions.question: How can Chrumko increase his productivity when doing homework?
options: Spend more time without changing anything
Turn off his phone, prepare his space and work concentrated
Study with friends without a plan
questions.explanation: Concentrated work in a quiet environment without distractions is key to higher productivity.
